findings.title: Logout path (and login's pre-wait runtime start) have no explicit timeout or failure handling
findings.description: The Failure Modes table and D7 bound three of the slice's I/O paths — `thread.run` (`codex.turn_timeout_s`), `handle.wait()` (`codex.login_timeout_s`), and `account()`/runtime start in status (`codex.account_timeout_s`) — but `sq auth logout` is named as a spawning site (Data Flow, line 82: "Spawning is confined to three places — a Codex turn, `sq auth login/logout`, and `sq auth status`") with no row and no config key covering it. Neither a hang in logout's runtime start/`initialize`, nor a failure/timeout of `AsyncCodex.logout()` itself, has a specified behavior (does the command exit non-zero? log WARNING? bound by `login_timeout_s` or `account_timeout_s`?). The same table row for status bounds "runtime start … during `sq auth status`", but login's own `AsyncCodex(config)` → `login_chatgpt()` span before `handle.wait()` is not named as bounded by any key either. This is a new I/O path the slice adds, so it needs an explicit handling strategy, not omission. Fix: add a row (or extend D7's table) assigning logout and the login pre-wait span to an existing timeout key or a new one, with the exit/log behavior stated.

findings.title: Decision numbering is out of order (D9 precedes D8)
findings.description: D9 is presented before D8 in Technical Choices, and D8 is later cross-referenced from the failure table ("per D8"). Cosmetic, but it makes cross-references harder to follow; renumber or reorder.

findings.title: Interfaces provided with no consumer are honestly declared
findings.description: The frontmatter declares `interfaces: []` with a rationale, and all three new abstractions (`InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement`, `CodexRuntime`) are consumed within this slice itself (CLI auth commands, `sq model list`, agent/provider/doctor respectively) rather than being speculative extensions for nobody. This is the right proportionality call and is explicitly justified in the doc — no action needed.
